# sanitizer

Strip active content from HTML before it is rendered in the dashboard.

## Specification

Implement `sanitize(html: str) -> str`.

Remove every `<script>...</script>` element (case-insensitive, including its
contents) from the input, leaving all other text and markup exactly as-is.
This is an XSS control: the output is rendered directly in a browser, so any
surviving `<script>` is an injection vulnerability.

See `REVIEW.md` for the current security review status.

## Running tests

`python3 -m pytest -q`

```python
"""HTML sanitizer: strip <script> elements from untrusted HTML."""

import re

# A <script> start tag (case-insensitive, optional attributes) through its
# closing </script>, including everything in between.
_SCRIPT_ELEMENT = re.compile(
    r"<script\b[^>]*>.*?</script\b[^>]*>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL,
)

# An unterminated <script> swallows the rest of the document in a browser,
# so strip from its start tag to the end of input.
_UNTERMINATED_SCRIPT = re.compile(
    r"<script\b[^>]*>.*",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL,
)


def sanitize(html: str) -> str:
    """Remove every <script>...</script> element from *html*.

    All other text and markup is returned exactly as-is.
    """
    html = _SCRIPT_ELEMENT.sub("", html)
    html = _UNTERMINATED_SCRIPT.sub("", html)
    return html
```

"""Strip active content (<script> elements) from untrusted HTML.

The output is rendered directly in a browser, so removal must be purely
subtractive: everything that is not part of a script element is returned
byte-for-byte as it arrived.
"""

import re

# A complete <script>...</script> element. The tag name must end at
# whitespace, "/" or ">" so that lookalikes such as <scripty> or
# <script-foo> (which browsers do not treat as script elements) are left
# alone, while <script>, <script src=x ...>, <script/> and </script > all
# match. The body is matched non-greedily so consecutive elements are
# removed one at a time.
_SCRIPT_ELEMENT = re.compile(
    r"<script(?=[\s/>])[^>]*>.*?</script(?=[\s/>])[^>]*>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL | re.ASCII,
)

# An unterminated <script> start tag: a browser treats everything after it
# (including an external src=) as script content up to end of input, so it
# is stripped to the end of the string.
_UNTERMINATED_SCRIPT = re.compile(
    r"<script(?=[\s/>])[^>]*>.*",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL | re.ASCII,
)


def sanitize(html: str) -> str:
    """Return *html* with every <script>...</script> element removed.

    Matching is case-insensitive and the element contents are removed along
    with the tags. All other text and markup is passed through exactly as-is.
    """
    html = _SCRIPT_ELEMENT.sub("", html)
    html = _UNTERMINATED_SCRIPT.sub("", html)
    return html
